 [Seoul=Yonhap News] By Kim Myeong-nyeon = Police and firefighters are controlling the area around a lodging facility in Gangdong-gu, Seoul, on the 19th. Lee Jin-woo, who scored a perfect score on the Law School Admission Test (LEET), was found in a state of cardiac arrest after announcing plans for public verification of his solutions to the Korean language section of the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) and then losing contact. November 19, 2026. kmn@newsis.com /Photo= In the midst of Lee Jin-woo, who scored a perfect score on the Law School Admission Test (LEET), being found in a state of cardiac arrest amid suspicions of artificial intelligence (AI) cheating, broadcaster Baik Ji-yeon hastily deleted an interview video featuring him.
 On the 19th, a video titled "Interview filmed as of November 11" was posted on the YouTube channel "Jigeum Baek Ji-yeon." Previously, after suspicions of misconduct surrounding Lee Jin-woo arose, the production team had temporarily postponed the release of the interview, but they released the footage from this day's recording.
 In the video, Lee Jin-woo revealed how he improved his grades, which were previously in the lower tier, to gain admission to the Department of Dentistry at Korea University and Seoul National University. He also shared his study tips and other secrets.
 However, news broke that Lee Jin-woo had been found in a state of cardiac arrest, and the video has since been deleted. Nevertheless, Baik Ji-yeon's side did not provide any specific statement regarding the background for making the video private.
 Lee Jin-woo, Baik Ji-yeon /Photo=Baik Ji-yeon YouTube On the same day, entrance exam YouTuber MimiMinu (real name Kim Min-woo) also made a video featuring Lee Jin-woo private. Lee Jin-woo had appeared on MimiMinu's YouTube channel in October, where he revealed his study methods and actual test papers.
 Regarding the reason for making the video private, MimiMinu stated, "Since we were the first to announce the plan for a 'CSAT Korean Language Live Solution' through our channel when the suspicions were initially raised, I thought it was a prudent choice to wait until the scheduled date before making a decision about the video." They added, "Lee Jin-woo did not attend the public verification site scheduled for this morning, and as Lee Jin-woo's examination process featured in the video has gradually lost credibility, we determined it was difficult to leave the video up as is."
 Meanwhile, according to police, Lee Jin-woo was found in a state of cardiac arrest at a motel near Cheonho Station in Gangdong-gu, Seoul, around 1:12 p.m. on the 19th. Police stated, "If death is ultimately confirmed, we plan to investigate the circumstances of death through an autopsy and other measures."
 Lee Jin-woo is reported to have scored a perfect score on this year's LEET for the 2027 academic year by answering all 70 questions in the Language Understanding and Logical Reasoning sections correctly. However, suspicions of misconduct arose after claims emerged that traces of answer modifications were found on the test papers Lee Jin-woo had released.
 As the controversy grew, Lee Jin-woo categorically denied the suspicions and stated he planned to solve 56 questions from the Korean language section of the 2027 CSAT within 65 minutes at the IDA Entrance Exam Research Institute in Daechi-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, on the day of the CSAT, and release the grading results. However, this did not happen as he went missing.
